chunks: Al-Naqid Abu al-Husayn Ahmad ibn 'Abdillah ibn 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to me from his father, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ghanawi, from Sulayman, who said:

Was there any angel left in the heavens who did not descend to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.a.w.) to console him regarding his son, al-Husayn (a.s.), and to inform him of Allah's reward for him, and to bring to him his dust, upon which he fell, was slaughtered, killed, wounded, thrown down, and abandoned?
The Messenger of Allah (s.a.a.w.) said: 'O Allah, abandon whoever abandoned him, kill whoever killed him, slaughter whoever slaughtered him, and do not let him enjoy what he sought.'
'Abd al-Rahman said: By Allah, the accursed Yazid was hastened [to his death], and he did not enjoy after his killing what he sought.
'Abd al-Rahman said: And he was taken suddenly; he spent the night drunk and became dead in the morning, changed, as if he were coated with tar. He was taken in grief.

And no one remained from those who followed him in his killing or who were in his fighting except that madness, leprosy, or whitening of the skin afflicted him, and that became an inheritance in their progeny.
ai.seo_question: What happened to Yazid and his followers after the killing of Husayn (a.s.) according to this narration?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the cosmic significance of Karbala by depicting the descent of all angels to console the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.) with the news of Husayn’s (a.s.) martyrdom, emphasizing the divine reward awaiting him. It concludes with a specific supplication for the abandonment and destruction of the killers, which Shia tradition interprets as literally fulfilled by the sudden, intoxicated death of Caliph Yazid and the hereditary afflictions (madness, leprosy) that plagued his lineage and followers.
